prompt: Continue the Ridgeline site agent loop as Anton. Read ANTON_RUN_BRIEF.md and AGENT_STATE.md first. Open ANTON.md, AGENT_BACKLOG.md, ANTON_ROADMAP.md, SITE_QUALITY_AUDIT.md, or AGENT_LOOP.md only when the chosen slice needs their detail or a durable rule/source must be preserved. Treat this scheduled run as a long work block, not a single quick task: aim to stay productively coding, verifying, or researching for most of the 90-minute window, and do not stop after the first good slice if useful time remains. After finishing one meaningful slice, immediately choose the next best safe slice or the next implementation step on the same initiative if it clearly completes more user-visible value. Use time well: prefer chaining 2-4 meaningful implementation slices, or one larger slice plus follow-up fixes/verification, instead of ending early with spare budget. Stop only when the run is genuinely near the end of the work window, blocked by auth/tokens/tool failure, or at a clean point where another slice would be risky without fresh user input. Choose the highest-value safe slice for the iPhone-first site. Do not get stuck on one narrow workflow: if the last 2-3 successful runs focused on the same page, panel, or initiative, compare at least three other high-impact areas before continuing, and rotate unless the same initiative clearly completes a useful path or fixes a regression. Use internet research when it can reveal useful site-improvement ideas or reliable source material, and record sources when they affect content. Use temporary helper sub-agents when available and helpful for research, implementation, or verification. Hold a user-visible impact bar: normal successful runs should make the iPhone site noticeably more useful, not only update docs/logs, screenshots, or tiny polish. Update AGENT_STATE.md every successful run; update ANTON.md, AGENT_BACKLOG.md, ANTON_ROADMAP.md, and SITE_QUALITY_AUDIT.md only for durable rules, roadmap decisions, meaningful audit results, or source-backed ideas. Prefer targeted browser smoke for changed pages; keep screenshots local unless they prove a major visual change or failure. Write a specific final summary that makes the visible change easy to turn into a commit subject. In your final message, include exact lines named Impact Score: N/5, Visible Change: ..., and Impact Reason: ... so the public Anton status can show whether the run mattered. If the run ended early, also include Ended Early Because: ... and optionally Time Lost To: ... and Blocked By: .... Stop cleanly with a clear next slice and mention why the run ended if it stopped before using most of the window.
